_descriptor_type: A type of descriptor. One of 'simulation', 'trace', and 'perf'.
_architecture: A name of the available architectures (PARAMS.<architecture>) found in scarab repository, which defines the machine parameters of the default configuration.
_experiment: The name of the experiment. scarab-infra will create a new folder named containing all files needed to execute the simulation in the <ROOT_DIR>/simulations/<experiment> directory. The folder will also contain all generated simulation statistics/outputs.
_workload_manager: manual: run each exp scenario with all the simpoints at a time, slurm: Slurm schedules simulations based on its policy
_root_dir: Root directory mounted into the docker container home, for instance, the user's home directory
_application_dir: The path to the benchmark application directory used for tracing or simulation.
_scarab_path: The path to the scarab repository that contains the scarab binary used to run the experiment. REQUIRES the build with the combined marked-RRPV policy and the two-axis MLC set duel (--td_combined_set_duel with td_combined_duel_basic_axis / td_combined_duel_basic_sets_per_group). PARAMS.google must also carry the bp_l0_latency 0 / bp_main_latency 1 fix -- with decode_cycles at the spec's 1 and the L0 early predictor left on, bp.c:213 asserts BP_MAIN_LATENCY < DECODE_CYCLES and the run dies at init.
_traces_dir: The local directory containing all simpointed traces
_top_simpoint: Run only top 3 simpoints stored in 'workloads_top_simp.json'.
_simulations: Deep follow-up to google_combined_l2 on the same google traces (12 workloads x 3 simpoints, memtrace) and the same 2 MB / 16-way / 2048-set L2. NO BASELINE CONFIG -- splice against google_combined_l2 (or plot with plot_stat_change_multi.py --raw, which needs no baseline). Four groups. (1) DEEPER LADDER depth_d96 extends past that run's d64 end, with narrow-gate twins at both 96 and 64 to test whether deep protection only pays once the gate is selective enough to keep the protected set small. (2) RATIOS ratio_i64d48 / ratio_i96d64 probe instruction-deeper-than-data at the deep end -- and note these bracket the MLC duel's own compiled bins (i72d48 / instr-only i96 / data-only d64), so the static points directly frame what the duel is choosing among. (3) repl_srrip is plain SRRIP on the L2, the unmarked parent of this whole policy family and the honest floor: marked-RRIP has to beat its own base mechanism, not just tree-PLRU. (4) SET DUELING duel_* lets the mechanism pick a depth bin per window instead of pinning one. At 2048 sets the leader tax is small -- 3x16 = 48 sets (2.3%) for the depth arm alone, 3x16+2x8 = 64 (3.1%) with the basic arm -- versus 12.5% on the old 512-set L2, so dueling is far cheaper here than it was.
_configurations: Naming: depth_d<N> = both classes at -N with the nominal gate (fe 0.7 / load 0.5); thresh_narrow_d<N> = the same depths with the narrow gate (fe 0.8 / load 0.6); ratio_i<N>d<M> = --td_fe_rrip_min_rrpv -N / --td_load_rrip_min_rrpv -M. CAUTION: --mlc_cache_repl_policy is silently IGNORED whenever --td_combined_on_mlc is set (init_memory picks REPL_MARKED_RRIP first), so the ordinal appears only on repl_srrip and must never be pasted onto a td_ config. For the duel_* configs the depth bins are COMPILED IN (g_duel_instr / g_duel_data in memory.c: i72d48, instruction-only i96, data-only d64), so --td_fe_rrip_min_rrpv / --td_load_rrip_min_rrpv have NO effect there and are omitted; the thresholds still apply. Group 0 of the duel always runs the incumbent so ties hold it, and exactly one coordinate moves per window.

depth_d96._params: Both classes at -96, nominal gate. Extends google_combined_l2's ladder past its d64 end.

thresh_narrow_d96._params: Both classes at -96 with the NARROW gate (fe 0.8 / load 0.6). One-variable delta from depth_d96: does very deep protection need a selective gate to avoid crowding the 16 ways?

thresh_narrow_d64._params: Both classes at -64 with the NARROW gate. One-variable delta from google_combined_l2's depth_d64 (which is -64 at the nominal gate), so the pair isolates the gate at a fixed depth.

ratio_i64d48._params: Instructions -64, data -48. Instruction-deeper-than-data at the deep end; matches the MLC duel's first compiled bin scaled down slightly.

ratio_i96d64._params: Instructions -96, data -64. Same 3:2 instruction:data ratio as ratio_i64d48, scaled up 1.5x -- so the pair separates the RATIO from the MAGNITUDE.

repl_srrip._params: Plain SRRIP (REPL_SRRIP, 16) on the L2 -- the unmarked parent of the marked-RRIP family and the honest floor for it. Marked-RRIP inserts at a negative RRPV and reuses srrip_update_evict for aging and eviction, so this is the same mechanism with the marking removed.

duel_depth._params: Set duel, DEPTH arm only (basic axis off): 3 leader groups x 16 sets = 48 of 2048 (2.3%). Picks per window among the compiled bins i72d48 / instruction-only i96 / data-only d64; unmarked lines stay at the global --marked_rrip_basic_rrpv default of 3.

duel_depth_basic._params: Set duel, DEPTH + BASIC arms: 5 leader groups (3x16 + 2x8) = 64 of 2048 (3.1%). Adds the unmarked-RRPV axis over {2,3,4} on top of the depth bins.

duel_depth_g8._params: Set duel, depth arm only, 8 sets per group = 24 leader sets (1.2%). Halves the sampling tax against duel_depth so more followers cash in the winner; noisier per-bin miss counts. The pair separates 'the duel picks well' from 'the leader tax costs'.

_collect_stats: Stats collection settings for ./sci --collect-stats. configs: optional list of configuration names to collect (null or omitted = all configurations).
_visualize: No baseline config exists in this run by design. Either splice with google_combined_l2 (plot_stat_change_multi.py takes several CSVs and resolves each config from whichever contains it) or use --raw, which needs no baseline at all. The baseline named below is only a placeholder so the field does not dangle.
_mem: Memory scheduling and collection settings for Slurm jobs.
